Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class DesktopTransparency

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.DesktopTransparency
public final class DesktopTransparency extends Object
Renders the 2D desktop's user-settable surface opacity, the engine behind the four TransparencySurface settings.

Fading a Swing component is not a matter of turning down its background alpha. A window hosts third-party panels that fill themselves opaque, and the taskbar paints over a wallpaper it does not own, so the shell - which is the only party that knows what is behind - has to do the fading. It does so by letting the component paint into a transparent scratch image and blitting that image back with AlphaComposite: the component keeps painting exactly as it always did, every pixel it produces keeps its own contrast, and the wallpaper shows through the gap left by the missing alpha. That works with any look-and-feel and needs no change inside the components being faded.

The engine caches the four opacities in memory, refreshed from DesktopConfig on the EDT at shell start-up and on every live apply (refresh()). Paint code reads the cache, never the preferences: a headless JVM, a running 3D desktop or a unit test that does not isolate java.util.prefs all keep the default - fully solid - instead of touching the preference store from a paint pass.

At the default of 100 percent nothing is composited at all; callers are expected to short-circuit on

invalid reference 
#isSolid(JComponent)
, which keeps the legacy paint path byte-identical and costs nothing for users who never open the setting.

  • Method Details

    • alphaFor

      public static float alphaFor(int opacityPercent)
      The alpha a surface painted at opacityPercent is blitted at: 100 is solid (1f), 0 invisible. Out-of-range input is clamped rather than rejected, because the value can come from a stored preference written by an older build.

    • isSolid

      public static boolean isSolid(int opacityPercent)
      Whether opacityPercent means "paint nothing special" - the pixel-identical legacy path, which every paint hook checks first.

    • fade

      public static Color fade(Color c, float alpha)
      c with its alpha scaled by alpha, keeping the colour itself intact: fade(Color.RED, 0.5f) is still red, at half alpha. Null passes through so paint hooks can chain it over an absent colour.

    • opacityOf

      public static int opacityOf(TransparencySurface surface)
      This surface's opacity as the shell is currently painting it, from the in-memory cache. The value paint code reads; see refresh() for how it is kept in step with the persisted configuration.

    • alphaOf

      public static float alphaOf(TransparencySurface surface)
      opacityOf(TransparencySurface) turned into a blit alpha.

    • allSolid

      public static boolean allSolid()
      Whether every surface is solid, i.e. whether any painting has to be composited at all. The desktop pane and the taskbar check this first so the default configuration keeps the stock paint path - and the stock pixels - untouched.

    • setOpacityFor

      public static void setOpacityFor(TransparencySurface surface, int percent)
      Writes one surface into the paint cache without touching the preference store, so a headless test or a preview can paint a faded desktop that is never persisted. Production code goes through applyOpacity(TransparencySurface, int), which stores the value first; anything applied here is overwritten by the next refresh().

    • refresh

      public static void refresh()
      Pulls the four persisted opacities into the paint cache. Must run on the EDT; called by the 2D shell when it starts and from Desktop2D.applyDesktopConfig(), which is what makes a control center slider take effect without a restart. Reading DesktopConfig is the only preferences access in this class, and it deliberately never happens during a paint.

    • applyOpacity

      public static void applyOpacity(TransparencySurface surface, int percent)
      Stores one surface's opacity in the persisted configuration and repaints the shell so it shows immediately. The control center's single write path for transparency: the save is what makes the choice survive a restart, and Desktop2D.applyDesktopConfig() is a no-op when the 2D desktop is not running, so the same call from a 3D session just stores the value for the next 2D start-up.
      Parameters:
      surface - which surface to fade
      percent - opacity as a percent of solid, clamped by DesktopConfig.MIN_SURFACE_OPACITY

    • isFaded

      public static boolean isFaded(Component child)
      Whether child is a desktop component that asks to be faded with one of the user's settings, i.e. whether its parent has to route it through paintFaded(Graphics2D, JComponent, float) instead of painting it the stock way. The opacity short-circuit lives here, so a surface left at the default never reaches the compositing code.

    • paintFaded

      public static void paintFaded(Graphics2D g, JComponent child, float alpha)
      Paints child into g at alpha instead of letting it paint directly. The child is rendered whole into a transparent scratch image - at its own bounds, offset by its location in the parent - and that image is blitted back with AlphaComposite.SRC_OVER, so what shows through the difference is whatever the parent had already painted.

      Must run on the EDT, like all painting. The caller's clip and rendering hints are carried into the scratch image so the child cannot tell it is being composited; antialiasing in particular stays as the parent set it.

      Parameters:
      g - the parent's graphics, in the parent's coordinate space
      child - the component to fade; skipped when it is not showing or, for an internal frame, when it is iconified - a minimised frame is painted by its desktop icon, not here
      alpha - blit alpha in 0..1. >= 1 paints the child straight onto g, so the caller may use this method unconditionally; <= 0 paints nothing at all
